name: Omali Yeshitela: 1966 City Hall mural custody

case.charges: 1966 St. Petersburg City Hall mural removal: destruction of city property and disorderly breach of the peace (municipal); grand larceny (state).
case.convicted: Municipal convictions; subsequent state grand-larceny conviction vacated by the U.S. Supreme Court on April 6, 1970 (Waller v. Florida).
case.sentence: Sentenced to 180 days in county jail on the municipal charges, then six months to five years on the state charge, with 170 days credited. At the November 13, 1969 Supreme Court argument, his lawyer reported 16 months already spent in jail and about 18 months out on bond. In a June 2016 press conference, Yeshitela recalled two and a half years in prison for the mural. These accounts do not establish a reconciled final custody total or exact release date. The Supreme Court vacated the state conviction on double-jeopardy grounds on April 6, 1970; that decision date is not a verified release date.

editorial_notes: Adds one historical case to the existing profile, covering both prosecutions of the same mural incident; does not edit any biography, website, photo, profile status, or existing case.

Do not store 16 or 30 in imprisoned_for_months: the schema treats that field as an unqualified final total. Sixteen months is reported as of the 1969 argument; thirty months is a later recollection. Preserve both with attribution in the case sentence instead.

Leave incarceration_date, release_date, sentenced_date and numeric custody counters unset. Arrest does not establish the start of a continuous custody interval, and neither an inferred bond date nor the Supreme Court decision is a verified release date.
Do not add the municipal sentence to the state sentence or add the 170-day credit to time served; the prosecutions overlap.
No institution assignment or coordinates: county confinement is established, but a specific historical facility has not been verified.
